THE TRANSITION, EXPLAINED

Old law. New law. Side by side.

A functional crosswalk—not a blind find-and-replace. The new criminal laws generally commenced on 1 July 2024.

Print comparison
Dates and ingredients matter. Savings, amendments, and transitional rules can affect the applicable law. Check BNS section 358, BNSS section 534, and the exact provision before relying on a mapping.
THE FORMER FRAMEWORKTHE CURRENT FRAMEWORKWHAT TO UNDERSTAND
General criminal lawIndian Penal Code, 1860SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

Reorganized offences, new numbering, and revised provisions.

Check conduct date and savings; the IT Act continues.
Criminal procedureCrPC, 1973SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNSS, 2023

Electronic processes and expanded audiovisual documentation.

Read transitional provisions and current notifications.
Evidence lawIndian Evidence Act, 1872SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBSA, 2023

Reorganized evidence rules and expanded electronic-record provisions.

Earlier judgments remain relevant only with the current text.
CheatingIPC 415 / 420SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNS 318 / 318(4)

General cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery framework.

Dishonest inducement and other elements still need proof.
PersonationIPC 416 / 419SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNS 319 / 319(2)

General personation framework; compare IT Act 66D separately.

A fake account alone does not prove every element.
ForgeryIPC 463 / 465SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNS 336

Express inclusion of false electronic records in the new wording.

Select the correct definition and punishment subsection.
Forgery for cheatingIPC 468SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNS 336(3)

Aggravated forgery linked to intended cheating.

Check the intended use and exact elements.
Use of forged documentIPC 471SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNS 340(2)

Fraudulent or dishonest use as genuine.

Knowledge and the forged character must be established.
ExtortionIPC 383 / 384SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNS 308

Threat-induced dishonest delivery framework.

Assess the threat and inducement, not just a payment demand.
Criminal breach of trustIPC 405 / 406SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNS 316

Entrustment and dishonest misappropriation framework.

Do not assume all data misuse satisfies the property elements.
ConspiracyIPC 120A / 120BSUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNS 61

Reorganized definition and punishment.

Shared infrastructure is not proof of agreement.
Common intentionIPC 34SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNS 3(5)

Acts in furtherance of common intention.

Apply the facts and the complete wording.
StalkingIPC 354DSUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNS 78

Repeated contact or monitoring framework.

Read the exceptions and establish the required pattern.
VoyeurismIPC 354CSUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNS 77

Private-image capture and dissemination protections.

Do not equate every photograph with the offence.
Criminal intimidationIPC 503 / 506SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNS 351

Threats and punishment organized in the new provision.

Choose the subsection matching the threat.
DefamationIPC 499 / 500SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNS 356

Definition, exceptions, and procedure reorganized.

Analyze publication, harm, and exceptions.
Production orderCrPC 91SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNSS 94

Broadly corresponding production power, with electronic-record language.

Production is not a general search or interception power.
FIR / cognizable informationCrPC 154SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNSS 173

Electronic information and specified preliminary enquiry.

Signature and other conditions remain important.
Witness examinationCrPC 161SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNSS 180

Broadly corresponding police examination framework.

Follow the applicable recording safeguards.
Magistrate-recorded statementsCrPC 164SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNSS 183

Broadly corresponding confession and statement procedure.

A technical expert is not automatically the recording authority.
Police searchCrPC 165SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNSS 185; also 105

Expanded audiovisual documentation framework.

Check the exact action, grounds, and recording requirements.
Police completion reportCrPC 173SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNSS 193

Investigation reporting and further-investigation framework.

BNSS 173 concerns a different subject from CrPC 173.
High Court inherent powersCrPC 482SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBNSS 528

Broadly corresponding inherent-power provision.

Use the current text and applicable precedent.
Expert opinionIEA 45SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBSA 39

Specialist opinion framework.

Expert status does not make every assertion conclusive.
Electronic-record proof routeIEA 65ASUCCEEDING PROVISIONBSA 62

Contents proved through the special electronic-record provision.

Read with the actual output and section 63.
Electronic outputIEA 65BSUCCEEDING PROVISIONBSA 63

Expanded wording for devices, networks, and electronic storage.

Not a mere renumbering; assess the new conditions.
Electronic certificateIEA 65B(4)SUCCEEDING PROVISIONBSA 63(4) + Schedule

Prescribed Part A / Part B form, party and expert signatures, hash particulars.

Do not relabel an old one-signature form as the new certificate.

The IT Act, 2000 continues as a special law. The DPDP Act, 2023 is a separate data-protection framework. Neither was replaced by the BNS.
